title: Finance operational scenarios checklist: commitment & contingency
author: Diego Martinez
body:
Summary:
This document is an operational checklist for cross-functional finance scenarios that commonly affect forecasting, procurement commitments, contract ingestion, and revenue recognition handoffs. It codifies decision thresholds, owner responsibilities, approval gates, and escalation paths for three high-impact scenarios: rapid usage ramp (hosted API/dedicated capacity), mid-contract price change requests, and supplier procurement delays that affect committed capacity.

Scope:
- Applies to all enterprise and dedicated-capacity commercial contracts, purchase orders (POs) that exceed $50k or any that create capital or recurring commitments, and procurement requests that could materially affect quarterly forecasts.
- Not intended for purely internal one-time purchases under $5k (use procurement self-serve).

Principles:
- Forecast accuracy matters: changes to committed spend must be reflected in the rolling 12-week cash and MRR forecast within two business days of approval.
- Single source of truth: the contract ingestion system (ContractDB) remains definitive for billing and revrec triggers.
- Fast, auditable decisions: every commitment action must be logged with approver, date, and reason.

Primary owners and contacts:
- Finance (Forecasting & RevRec): Evelyn Cho (forecast_owner@redwood.example), backup: Maya Singh.
- Procurement: Liam O'Connor (procurement_lead@redwood.example).
- Legal (Commercial Contracts): Priya Raman (legal_contracts@redwood.example).
- Sales / Customer Success: account executive or CSM owning the customer relationship.

Scenario matrix (decision table):
| Scenario                                | Trigger threshold                         | Required approvals                         | Forecast action                      |
|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| Rapid usage ramp (hosted API)          | >20% week-over-week growth or +$100k/mo   | Finance + Sales lead                        | Reforecast immediate 12-week cadence  |
| Dedicated capacity commit              | Contracted GPU commit > $250k annualized  | Finance + Procurement + Legal               | Add to committed revenue queue (RevRec) |
| Supplier delay affecting delivery      | Delay > 30 days or < 80% capacity         | Procurement + Engineering + Finance        | Apply contingency buffer, notify sales |

Procedures (step-by-step):
1) Pre-commit approval (for any new commitment > $50k):
   1.1 Sales or Product submits Commitment Request Form (Confluence link + ContractDB stub).
   1.2 Procurement validates vendor terms and lead time.
   1.3 Finance runs cash-impact and P&L sensitivity (3 scenarios: base, -20% revenue, +30% cost).
   1.4 Legal reviews commercial terms for data/residency/KMS/HIPAA clauses.
   1.5 Approval: Finance director and Procurement lead must countersign; Legal signs if contractual exceptions exist.
   1.6 Upon approval, Procurement creates PO and uploads signed contract into ContractDB; update forecast spreadsheet and internal dashboards.

2) Forecast update cadence and artifacts:
   - Triggered updates: within 2 business days after any approval or material amendment.
   - Weekly rolling forecast: 12-week rolling forecast updated every Friday EOD and published to Finance dashboard.
   - Required artifacts: signed contract, PO number, projected monthly burn schedule, capacity mapping (if hardware), and revrec trigger mapping.

3) Contract ingestion to billing & RevRec mapping (checklist):
   - Verify contract exists in ContractDB with correct effective and term dates.
   - Confirm billing cadence (monthly/quarterly/annual) in contract metadata.
   - Map contract line items to billing codes and billing service identifiers used by BillingEngine.
   - Mark revrec trigger: performance obligations identified and assigned to RevRec owner.
   - File an ingestion ticket to BillingOps with contract id and expected first invoice date.

Escalation & exception matrix:
| Issue                                  | Escalation chain (1 -> 2 -> 3)            | SLA for resolution                         |
|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| Contract ingestion mismatch             | BillingOps -> Finance RevRec -> Legal     | 3 business days                            |
| Unplanned cost overrun (>15% of PO)    | Procurement -> Finance -> COO             | 2 business days                            |
| Customer requests early termination    | Sales -> Legal -> Finance                 | 5 business days                            |

Operational examples (sample run):
- Example A: Customer requests dedicated 50-GPU pool; procurement estimates 8-week lead time and $420k annual. Flow: Sales opens Commitment Request -> Procurement validates vendor -> Finance models cash impact -> Legal approves terms with KMS clause -> Approvals captured -> PO issued -> Contract ingested -> Forecast updated.

Metrics and SLOs to track (finance dashboard):
- Time from approval to forecast update: target <= 2 business days.
- Contract ingestion lag (signed -> BillingEngine ticket): target <= 3 business days.
- % of monthly variance explained by committed changes: target > 90% (explainable activity).
- Number of unapproved commitments discovered in audits: target 0.

Templates, CLI snippets, and config examples:
- Commitment Request minimal fields (CSV/JSON):
  customer_name,contract_id,product_line,annual_value,po_number,effective_date,term_months,owner,email

- Minimal revrec mapping example (JSON rendered inline):
  {
    "contract_id": "C-2026-0153",
    "line_items": [
      {
        "sku": "DED-GPU-50",
        "billing_code": "gpu_dedicated_v1",
        "revrec_trigger": "service_commencement"
      }
    ]
  }

- BillingEngine ingestion CLI (example):
  $ billingctl ingest --contract C-2026-0153 --first-invoice 2026-06-01 --owner finance@redwood.example

Audit and retrospectives:
- Quarterly audits: Finance will run a committed-spend vs. recognized revenue audit and publish variance notes.
- Postmortem: if a commitment causes >$200k unplanned cost or >10% forecast miss, run a cross-functional postmortem within two weeks.

Related pages and references:
- Procurement: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/procurement-supplier-onboarding-and-invoice-routing-2026
- RevRec runbooks: /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/commitment-usage-reconciliation-sop-2026
- Contract ingestion standards: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contract-amendment-billing-cutoff-and-rev-trigger-guidance-2026

Appendix: quick checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Commitment Request submitted
- [ ] Procurement vendor validation complete
- [ ] Finance cash/P&L sensitivity attached
- [ ] Legal exceptions resolved or waived
- [ ] Approvals recorded (Finance, Procurement, Legal as required)
- [ ] PO and contract uploaded to ContractDB
- [ ] BillingEngine ingestion ticket filed
- [ ] Forecast updated (12-week and monthly models)

Document maintenance:
- Owner: Finance forecasting team. Review cadence: annual or when major billing/process changes occur.

Feedback: send suggested edits via the Confluence comment thread or email forecast_owner@redwood.example.
